entries.title: Gratitude.com Platform Model — Three-Sided Marketplace
entries.content: Gratitude.com is a three-sided impact technology platform. Sponsors (companies) fund impact through sponsorship. Activators (people) activate gratitude through action. Impact Partners (nonprofits/causes) receive delivered impact. This is NOT a donation platform — it's an activation engine.

entries.title: Five Key Differentiators
entries.content: 1) Real activation, not passive donation — people participate. 2) Instant delivery at scale — technology-driven. 3) Measurable outcomes — every act documented. 4) Corporate sponsorship model — brands fund impact, not individuals. 5) Bridges corporate CSR and personal meaning.

entries.title: Tone by Channel — Context-Specific Voice
entries.content: Sponsor comms: strategic, ROI-forward, partnership language. Activator messaging: warm, empowering, action-oriented. Nonprofit/partner: respectful, collaborative, impact-focused. Website: confident, conversion-focused, emotionally resonant. Social: punchy, inspiring, shareable. Impact reports: data-forward, credibility-first. Ads: problem-aware, benefit-led, strong CTA.

entries.title: Key Brand Phrases
entries.content: Five core phrases to use across all content: 1) "Gratitude isn't just felt. It's delivered." 2) "Activate gratitude as a force for good" 3) "Companies sponsor. People activate. Impact is delivered." 4) "Turn gratitude into action" 5) "Delivered into the world instantly and at scale."

entries.title: Terminology Rules — Words We Use vs. Words We Don't
entries.content: Always say "activate" not "donate." Say "sponsor" not "fund." Say "activator" not "donor/user." Say "impact" not "charity." Say "delivered" not "distributed." Say "activation" not "transaction." Say "impact partner" not "charity/beneficiary." Say "sponsor kit" not "media kit." Say "impact report" not "annual report." Always include .com in "Gratitude.com."

entries.title: Messaging by Stakeholder — Sponsors
entries.content: For sponsors (corporate partners): Your CSR budget deserves real outcomes. Not a logo on a banner. Not a line item in an annual report. Gratitude.com turns your sponsorship into activated impact that people participate in, documented with real numbers you can report to your board.

entries.title: Messaging by Stakeholder — Nonprofits
entries.content: For nonprofits (impact partners): Stop chasing individual donors. Gratitude.com connects you with corporate sponsors and activated communities at scale. Reliable funding, real participation, documented outcomes.

entries.title: Content Guardrails — What We Never Do
entries.content: Never claim grandiose impact without data. Never guarantee ROI on social impact. Never sound like a charity asking for donations, a tech startup overhyping, a corporate CSR press release, or a vague wellness brand. Never be sycophantic in sponsor comms. Never send deliverables without clear next steps. No passive voice in CTAs. No filler openers like "Hope this finds you well." Never guilt activators into action — inspire them.

entries.title: Social Platform Dimensions Quick Reference
entries.content: Instagram post square: 1080x1080 (60px safe zones). Instagram portrait: 1080x1350. Instagram story: 1080x1920 (top 200px and bottom 280px are UI zones). LinkedIn landscape: 1200x627 (40px safe zones). Facebook post: 1200x630. X/Twitter: 1200x675. YouTube thumbnail: 1280x720 (bottom-right has timestamp). Carousel: 1080x1080 per slide. Logo placement: bottom-right, 40px margin, max 120px wide.

entries.title: Agent Workflow Chains — Marketing + Design Pipelines
entries.content: Key pipelines: Social content with graphics = content-atomizer → social-creative. Landing page with design = direct-response-copy → web-mockup. Lead magnet PDF = lead-magnet → deliverable-design. Sponsor kit = direct-response-copy → deliverable-design. Full campaign = positioning-angles → direct-response-copy → content-atomizer → social-creative + deliverable-design. Newsletter distribution = newsletter → content-atomizer → social-creative.

entries.title: Email Sequence Types Available
entries.content: Five sequence types: 1) Sponsor welcome (5 emails) — onboarding new corporate sponsors. 2) Activator welcome (4 emails) — engaging new activators. 3) Partner onboarding (5 emails) — nonprofit partner setup. 4) Sales sequence (7 emails) — sponsor acquisition. 5) Nurture sequence — ongoing engagement. All follow voice-core rules: no filler openers, clear next steps, action-oriented CTAs.

entries.title: Channel-to-Message Map
entries.content: Website homepage: lead with value prop, support with platform model + social proof. Sponsor landing pages: lead with ROI, support with case studies. Activator pages: lead with ease and meaning, support with impact stories. LinkedIn: impact data or insight. Instagram: visual impact stories. Email to sponsors: one measurable outcome. Email to activators: one impact story. Ads: problem-aware hook. Impact reports: result headline. Partner decks: platform model + differentiation.

entries.title: 3-week social rollout framework with platform-specific audience targeting
entries.content: A successful social media rollout can be executed in just 3 weeks by focusing on 3 key platforms with distinct audiences: Instagram/TikTok for potential activators and LinkedIn for sponsors/partners. The strategy should progress from foundation building (week 1) to amplification (week 2) to conversion (week 3).

entries.title: Three-sided platform explanation works as repeatable content framework
entries.content: The 'companies sponsor → people activate → we deliver' framework provides clear, digestible explanation of complex platform mechanics. This pattern can be reused across different content types while maintaining clarity and consistency.

entries.title: Email signature design follows mobile-first, multi-platform approach
entries.content: Email signatures should use safe fonts (Arial, Helvetica, Calibri) with brand font fallbacks, maintain 600px max width for mobile optimization, and include both HTML and plain text versions. The design incorporates brand colors strategically with logo placement optimized for cross-platform compatibility.

entries.title: Sponsor Program Social Template Specs
entries.content: 1080x1080px Instagram/LinkedIn square format with dark premium background, signature pink-to-orange glow effect, and reserved negative space top-center for headline and bottom-right for logo placement (40px margin, max 120px wide). Uses Anton for headlines and Inter for supporting text with white logo treatment.

entries.title: Sponsor Program Messaging Needs Core Announcement Copy
entries.content: Social announcement graphics require clear headline and supporting CTA copy as critical components. Suggested messaging angles include 'SPONSOR REAL IMPACT' or program-specific names with supporting lines like 'Companies sponsor. People activate. Impact is delivered.' and CTAs like 'Become a Sponsor'.

entries.title: Dual structure: Gratitude.com PBC + ActivateGratitude.org 501(c)(3)
entries.content: Gratitude.com is a Public Benefit Corporation that builds the platform (technology, enterprise customers, consumer experience, revenue, scale). ActivateGratitude.org is a 501(c)(3) public charity that activates impact (receives donations, funds nonprofit partners, delivers verified acts). One creates enterprise value, the other creates public trust.

entries.title: Founder and investor contact: Michael Hilf
entries.content: Michael Hilf is Founder & CEO of Gratitude.com. Investor contact: mhilf@gratitude.com. All investor materials carry the footer: Michael Hilf, Founder & CEO, mhilf@gratitude.com, GRATITUDE.COM.

entries.title: Investor positioning: the Human Acknowledgment category
entries.content: Investor narrative positions Gratitude.com as category creation, not competition: the first platform turning gratitude into measurable impact, building shared behavioral infrastructure for human acknowledgment. AI angle: AI will reshape how we work; Gratitude.com will reshape how we connect.

entries.title: Flagship mechanic for investors: Tell Them (Express, Activate, Multiply)
entries.content: The flagship experience: Express (send a message to someone who changed your life), Activate (a pre-funded act of real-world impact triggers instantly through trusted nonprofit partners), Multiply (the recipient experiences both and is inspired to Tell Them). Tagline: Every message changes two lives.

entries.title: Market frames used with investors: $600B+ and $500B+
entries.content: Approved market frames: Wellbeing and employee engagement spend $600B+ (the budgets already exist) and social impact and philanthropy $500B+ (connecting existing capital, not creating a new market). Expansion path: individuals to organizations to communities to institutions.

entries.title: 24-month roadmap shown to investors
entries.content: Launch (60-90 days): MVP live, first enterprise customers, first nonprofit partners. Validate (months 1-6): thousands of verified activations, demonstrated enterprise value, proven repeatable model. Scale (18-24 months): millions of participants, global nonprofit ecosystem, category leadership. Framing: this round proves the model, the next scales it.

entries.title: Investor voice rules
entries.content: Investor-facing materials use a credibility-and-numbers voice: confident, declarative, zero hype qualifiers, US spelling (acknowledgment), no em dashes. Never invent metrics, traction, valuations, or projections; anything not in brand-kit/investor-core.yaml is [NEEDS INPUT].

entries.title: Pair activism visuals with impact-first captions
entries.content: When posting images of volunteer builds or sponsor activations, structure captions to lead with quantifiable impact metrics (homes built, families housed) before explaining the sponsorship role. This sequencing prioritizes the outcome story.

entries.title: Diverse representation in community action visuals
entries.content: Effective community building imagery should feature mixed ages, genders, and ethnicities working together in real hands-on scenarios. This authenticity resonates better than staged setups for activation and sponsorship storytelling.

entries.title: Request platform specifications before creative production
entries.content: Asking upfront where an image will be used (Instagram, sponsor deck, web banner) enables better composition choices and crop ratios. This prevents rework and ensures the creative fits its intended context perfectly.

entries.title: Position as acceleration layer, not replacement infrastructure
entries.content: When pitching to sophisticated corporate sponsors already running mature programs, frame the product as making existing commitments activate faster and prove themselves in real time. Avoid problem-agitation framing. JPMorgan doesn't need convincing to do CSR; they need proof that Gratitude.com instruments and accelerates what they already believe in.

entries.title: Before/after comparison resonates more than education for aware buyers
entries.content: For enterprise sponsors familiar with platform models, a two-column before/after slide (Today vs. With Gratitude.com) outperforms educational content. Lead with respect for what they're already doing, then show incremental gains in speed, documentation, and real-time reporting.
